title: Cyclone Akvan crosses coast near Gopalpur; Odisha reports no major damage or deaths
dek: The storm made landfall between 7.30 am and 8.30 am on Friday with winds of 70-80 kmph and is weakening over Odisha. About 3.7 lakh people were evacuated; heavy rain is forecast for Odisha, Jharkhand and south Bengal.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclone Akvan crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur in Odisha's Ganjam district between 7.30 am and 8.30 am on Friday, with maximum sustained winds of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said, and the Odisha government said there had been no major damage or loss of life so far.

"No damage or untoward incident has been reported so far," Odisha's Special Relief Commissioner, Rajesh Prabhakar Patil, said, according to reports, after about 3.7 lakh people had been moved out of low-lying and vulnerable areas over the week. The IMD expects the storm to weaken into a deep depression by about 11.30 am and into a depression by the evening as it moves north-north-east across Odisha, but has warned of heavy to very heavy rain in Odisha, Jharkhand and Gangetic West Bengal on Friday and a moderate risk of flash floods in ten south Bengal districts.

## What happened

In its 8.30 am bulletin, issued at noon, the IMD said the storm had moved north-north-west at 26 kmph over the previous six hours and "crossed the north Andhra Pradesh & south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur (near latitude 19.1 & longitude 84.8)". At 8.30 am its centre lay over south coastal Odisha close to Gopalpur, about 120 km north-east of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 130 km west-south-west of Puri and 230 km north-east of Visakhapatnam. The bulletin kept a red message for the coasts as a post-landfall outlook.

The storm had weakened overnight from a severe cyclonic storm and was weaker at landfall than the 90-100 kmph the IMD had forecast as late as Thursday night. Manorama Mohanty of the Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar said the landfall process began at about 8 am and would continue until about noon, according to reports.

Ganjam took the heaviest rain. Patrapur recorded 209 mm, Hinjili 207 mm, Chikiti 199 mm, Gopalpur 190 mm and Chhatrapur 139 mm, according to reports. Odisha's Disaster Management Minister, Suresh Pujari, said no major damage or loss of life had been reported, and Chief Secretary Anu Garg said: "There has been no major impact of the winds although rainfall has occurred under the influence of the cyclone," according to reports. In Andhra Pradesh, a state disaster management official described the impact as minimal, according to reports.

The IMD's forecast table has the storm's winds falling to 55-65 kmph by 11.30 am, 25-35 kmph by 5.30 pm, when it is expected to be a depression over northern Odisha, and 15-25 kmph by 11.30 pm, when it should have weakened into a well-marked low-pressure area near the Odisha-Jharkhand border.

## Evacuation and preparations

Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed preparations at the Special Relief Commissioner's office in Bhubaneswar from about 11 pm on Thursday until about 1.30 am on Friday and directed officials to work towards a "zero-casualty" target, according to reports. After the review, the state said preparations covered 20 districts and that more than 3 lakh people had been moved, up from 46,701 on Thursday morning; by Friday morning the figure was about 3.7 lakh, with 423 rescue teams deployed, according to reports.

According to the figures released after the review, 4,170 pregnant women close to their due dates were moved to health facilities, of whom 1,317 have given birth. Of 9,341 cyclone shelters readied, 2,623 were in use. The state has deployed 418 teams: 60 of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, 14 of the National Disaster Response Force, 216 fire service teams and 128 tree-cutting teams of the Odisha Forest Development Corporation, with 28 more fire service teams on standby.

The Department of Telecommunications has switched on intra-circle roaming in six districts, Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur and Khordha, until midnight on Friday, letting phones use any operator's network, according to the Odisha government.

## Warnings for Friday and Saturday

- Rain: heavy to very heavy at isolated places over Odisha, Jharkhand and Gangetic West Bengal on Friday; heavy at isolated places over Gangetic West Bengal and Jharkhand on Saturday, and over sub-Himalayan West Bengal on both days
- Flash floods: moderate risk over the next 24 hours in Gajapati, Ganjam, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Puri, Balasore, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Sambalpur, Sundargarh and Deogarh in Odisha; Bankura, Purulia, West Midnapore, East Midnapore, Howrah, North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas, Hooghly, Nadia and Purba Bardhaman in Bengal; and seven districts of Jharkhand
- Wind: gales of 60-70 kmph gusting to 80 kmph along the south Odisha coast, easing to 40-50 kmph by the evening; squally winds of 45-55 kmph gusting to 65 kmph along the north Odisha and Bengal coasts until Friday evening
- Fishermen: not to go into the west-central Bay of Bengal until Friday night or the north-west Bay of Bengal until Saturday morning
- North-east: heavy rain at isolated places over Manipur, Tripura, Mizoram and south Assam on Friday, and over Assam and Meghalaya too on Saturday

## Bengal

South Bengal is on the wetter side of the storm's track as the remnant moves north towards Jharkhand. The Regional Meteorological Centre in Kolkata had forecast 7-20 cm at one or two places in South 24 Parganas, East Midnapore, West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura until 8.30 am on Saturday, and 7-11 cm in Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, North 24 Parganas and Purulia. The Kolkata Municipal Corporation has put its control room on round-the-clock watch for waterlogging, fallen trees and damaged buildings, according to reports. South Eastern Railway cancelled at least 28 express trains for Friday, mostly to or through Puri, including the Howrah-Puri-Howrah Vande Bharat Express, according to reports.

## Background

Akvan is the third cyclone of the post-monsoon season in the Bay of Bengal and the third to threaten the same stretch of coast in about four weeks, after Arnab in late October and Murasu at the start of November. Its forecast track shifted several times this week: the IMD moved the expected crossing south, to between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, by Tuesday evening, then back north to the Narsapur-Puri stretch on Wednesday, and lowered the expected strength at landfall more than once. The storm slowed to about 5 kmph on Wednesday night before speeding up towards the coast. Murasu, which crossed near Ongole on 3 November, damaged crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 Andhra districts, according to the state government. IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said on Thursday that the exact landfall point and impact would depend on the storm's movement.

Odisha's evacuation-first approach dates from the 1999 super cyclone, which killed about 10,000 people in the state. Since then the state has built a network of cyclone and flood shelters and moves people to them before a storm arrives.

## What happens next

People will begin returning from shelters once district administrations declare it safe, and damage assessments of crops, houses and power lines are expected over the weekend. The heaviest rain moves north into interior Odisha, Jharkhand and south-west Bengal on Friday afternoon and night as the system weakens, before easing on Saturday. The IMD's next bulletins will track the remnant low.
